repositoryStructure.overview: A standard-go project of 238 files organized into 6 top-level directories (.githooks, .github, cmd, docs, infra, internal), separating entry points, business logic, infrastructure, and documentation.

architecture.overview: An event-driven, AWS-native system built from 4 major components on AWS IAM, AWS Lambda, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon EC2, Amazon EventBridge. A standard-go project of 238 files organized into 6 top-level directories (.githooks, .github, cmd, docs, infra, internal), separating entry points, business logic, infrastructure, and documentation.

components.name: Domain packages
components.responsibility: Business logic behind small, testable ports

architecture.deploymentTopology: A modular, multi-stack CloudFormation deployment: 16 serverless, 2 compute, 3 storage, and 8 networking resources, with least-privilege IAM (9 roles/policies).
architecture.scalability: Stateless Lambda entry points scale horizontally with request volume.
architecture.reliability: Reliability comes from managed, self-healing Lambda execution.
architecture.security: Security is enforced through least-privilege IAM roles, secrets stored in AWS Secrets Manager (never in code), HMAC-verified webhooks.
insights: The pipeline is fully event-driven: EventBridge Scheduler → Lambda → EC2 start/stop.
It blends serverless ingestion with an on-demand compute host, bounding cost while keeping the front door always available.
113 architecture diagram(s) document the system, aiding onboarding and technical writing.

whatChanged: feat(webhook): GitHub webhook automation via Lambda and EventBridge
implementation.howItWorks: An event-driven, AWS-native system built from 4 major components on AWS IAM, AWS Lambda, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon EC2, Amazon EventBridge. A standard-go project of 238 files organized into 6 top-level directories (.githooks, .github, cmd, docs, infra, internal), separating entry points, business logic, infrastructure, and documentation.
infrastructureImprovements: 9 CloudFormation template(s) define 57 resources across CloudWatch, EC2, Events, IAM, Lambda, Logs, S3, Scheduler, SecretsManager (16 serverless, 2 compute, 3 storage, 8 networking, 9 IAM, 10 messaging), with 65 parameters and 33 outputs.
implementation.whyItMatters: This advances the platform with new capability while keeping the existing contract stable.

technicalHighlights: feat(webhook): GitHub webhook automation via Lambda and EventBridge
infrastructureHighlights: 9 CloudFormation template(s) define 57 resources across CloudWatch, EC2, Events, IAM, Lambda, Logs, S3, Scheduler, SecretsManager (16 serverless, 2 compute, 3 storage, 8 networking, 9 IAM, 10 messaging), with 65 parameters and 33 outputs.
AWS services in use: AWS IAM, AWS Lambda, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon EC2, Amazon EventBridge, Amazon EventBridge Scheduler, Amazon S3.
A modular, multi-stack CloudFormation deployment: 16 serverless, 2 compute, 3 storage, and 8 networking resources, with least-privilege IAM (9 roles/policies).
architectureHighlights: The pipeline is fully event-driven: EventBridge Scheduler → Lambda → EC2 start/stop.
It blends serverless ingestion with an on-demand compute host, bounding cost while keeping the front door always available.
113 architecture diagram(s) document the system, aiding onboarding and technical writing.
Architectural patterns: Event-driven architecture, Serverless, Infrastructure as Code, Least-privilege security.
